The record — numbers, not adjectives

Four Portfolios, One Method: Exit Planned Before Entry

Every figure below is a real position. The first is our own.

01 Our own portfolio

Edmund Tan & Cindior Ho

We eat our own cooking.

  • Before10+ years in a sub-$600K HDB flat, capital sitting still.
  • AfterTre Ver 2BR bought at $1.05M, sold at $1.28M → laddered into a $3M property in under 4 years. Parc Clematis 2BR bought at $1.15M, sold at $1.525M over 3 years. Portfolio today: $5M+.
  • LessonThe flat wasn’t the problem — staying in it was. Every rung was chosen for its exit before we entered.
02

Edward & Rose

The upgrade that feels best often costs the most.

  • BeforeOn the verge of a “comfort upgrade” — the emotionally satisfying home that quietly ends a portfolio.
  • AfterSkipped it, followed the ladder, booked $500K+ in gains over 4 years and crossed $3.5M net asset value.
  • LessonThe math disagreed with the feeling — the math was right.
03

MoK & Jine

Structure beats size.

  • Before15 years in a ~$600K 4-room HDB flat, one asset, no plan.
  • AfterSplit into two 3-bedroom units — a ~$1.2M home to stay in and a ~$1M unit that rents. Rental offsets the loans, 8 years of reserves kept intact, $235K+ in gains, portfolio now past $3M.
  • LessonOne flat became two assets that pay for themselves.
04

Win / Esther & Family

Confidence is what’s left once the numbers remove the guesswork.

  • BeforeFearful and lost — too many opinions, no framework, paralysed on a decision they couldn’t afford to get wrong.
  • AfterA 1-on-1 plan, data-driven filtering of the field, and a confident purchase of an $1.8M unit aligned with their future moves.
  • LessonConfidence isn’t a personality trait. It’s what’s left once the numbers have removed the guesswork.
